Every removal is logged in Activity, unwatching and deleting a personal view included.

Every removal shows a message with an Undo button for 10 seconds, which puts back every record it changed (what it handed over or moved included). Admins restore anything removed, stopped, ended or marked as left in the last 30 days from Recently removed on Workspace, which shows the kind, the name, who removed it, when, and Restore; after 30 days it leaves the list but the row stays. The AI assistant has list_removed and restore_removed.

An admin marks someone as left from a dialog that first asks who takes over their goals and their open asks (as asker and as responder); they vanish from pickers, counts, review people and Home, their token no longer works, and history keeps their name as “Name (left)”. Someone with no goals, check-ins, notes or asks is deleted outright instead.

The owner or an admin stops a goal with check-ins, with a required reason: it leaves stats, reviews, Home, Watching and attention lists but stays on its page (marked Stopped, a shape and a word, as it stood but with no forecast: no “will it hit?” and no projection), in its history, in exports and in Activity; the goals feeding it move up to its parent and its open asks are withdrawn with a note. A goal with no check-ins is deleted instead.

One spreadsheet format: every sheet and column is defined once (src/domain/columns.ts), with its header, its meaning, whether it matches the row, can be changed or is worked out, and how it is written and read. The workbook, the zipped CSVs, one CSV, the set-up template, set-up from a spreadsheet, Import, the Data tables, the AI assistant’s tools and docs/export-format.md (checked to be current) are all made from it. Sheets are known by their header rows, never their names; CSV is read in one RFC 4180 pass (quotes, line breaks in a cell, a byte-order mark) and the formula guard’s apostrophe is taken off; worked-out columns use the vocabulary’s words and are never read; a word a column doesn’t know is a problem, never a default.

Whatever is exported loads straight back as no change: every demo workspace as a workbook and as zipped CSVs, on any day and at any number of decimal places (a number counts as typed only when it differs from what the export wrote), a Data table saved with columns hidden (its key columns are always written, greyed, at the end), and the AI assistant’s export_table into bulk_change. An edited copy applies exactly its edits, a line break or a leading “-” included. Goals are matched by key, then ID, so last cycle’s file still finds its goals; people by email, then a name only one person has, noted in the preview; every column that can be changed counts, and one a table leaves out keeps what the record says.

Every column a person can fill in says whether a new row must have it, its format, an example and what an empty cell means, in one list that the template, the workbook’s first sheet, Help, the import’s preview and the goal form are made from.

Every problem an import finds is Must fix, Check or fine. Must fix blocks saving; a Check is a question that must be answered; a problem is said once per kind with its count, and one answer covers every row with the same question. A near miss is asked about, never guessed and never silently refused.

Before anything is saved an import says which sheets and columns it read and which it did not, then counts by sheet, then what must be fixed, then its questions, then the changes on request with before and after and every default it used. Saving is all or nothing unless the person chooses to leave named rows out.

A spreadsheet given at set-up is checked before the read-back, not after it: every row that is wrong or doubtful is named with its row and its fix, counts never leave a wrong row out, the file's people join those typed, and nothing is saved until the workspace is created.

A spreadsheet’s Action column stops a goal with check-ins (with a Reason) or deletes one with none, and marks someone as left (their goals, open asks and teams going to Takes over, by email), with the same rules, refusals and consequences as the app (domain/removal), shown in the preview. The import’s Undo puts every one back: the goal live again, the deleted goal restored, the person back with their goals, asks, reviews and teams.

Every person has an email, kept lower case and unique in the workspace (migration 0027): required when someone is added, in Workspace, set-up, a spreadsheet or the AI assistant. Exports write each person’s name and email, and imports match people by email. People added before emails are listed on Workspace for an admin to fill in, together. The example’s people have example emails (firstname.lastname@example.com).

Every import, bulk edit and bulk change through MCP is one line in Past imports and one entry in Activity, and can be undone as a whole by whoever made it or an admin. Undo says beforehand which rows have changed since and will stay.

The import states its size limits before a file is chosen, checks a large file without freezing the page and shows progress, never draws more than a page of rows, and refuses to save more than it can save safely, with a way through. Saving tens of thousands of rows is a server-side job (R-L1 to R-L6).

Faro is a small core with named extension points (routes, navigation, Home blocks, goal-page sections, settings, places on core screens, database tables, AI tools, Help articles, requirements and journeys) and feature modules, one folder each with a module.json a generator can read, saying what it adds and what it needs. An admin switches each module on or off for a workspace on Workspace, Features (migration 0030): off, it leaves every screen, its AI tools refuse, and what needs it goes off too; nothing it saved is lost, and each switch is logged. CI builds Faro with each module left out and runs the core journeys, and a lint keeps src/domain free of database, screen and network code and the core from importing a module.

An admin switches Reviews off for a workspace. Off, there is no Reviews in the menu, on Home, on a goal or in the AI’s tools; asks and next steps are unchanged; what was said in reviews stays in history. Nothing is deleted, and switching it on restores it.

An admin chooses the check-in rhythm for a workspace: every week, or none. With none, nothing is due or late for want of a check-in, no goal reads No recent update, and a status that isn’t this week’s says which week it is from. Dates people set still count. The change says what it will do first, is logged, and can be undone.

The day check-ins are due never needs a review. One rule names the deadline: “before Thursday’s review” only when Reviews is on and a review is held that day, otherwise “by Thursday”, so with Reviews off no screen, receipt or count calls the deadline a review. Switching Reviews off says first that check-ins are still due by that day and how many accepted risks stay on their goals; a spreadsheet leaves out what is Reviews’ and an import says once that it wasn’t read; every switched-off module’s AI tools answer with one sentence; and back on, a session whose date passed while it was off is not “Not held yet”.

An admin switches Watching off for a workspace. Off, there is no Watching tab, no “Goals you watch”, no Watch button and no watching tool; someone who owns no goal is led to the goals that need attention. Switching it off first says how many people’s watches are kept. Every watch is kept, and switching it on restores each person’s.

A workspace defines up to six of its own fields on goals (a stage, a programme), each a list of values or free text, on Workspace, Fields: admins add, rename, reorder, retire and bring them back; everyone reads them. A goal's page shows one line per field in About, which its owner or an admin changes in place, and History says the change (“Stage: Discover → Build”). No rule reads a field; an AI assistant lists and sets them under the same rules.

An admin switches Fields off for a workspace. Off, a goal's page has no Fields block, Workspace has no Fields section (its address says Fields is switched off), and the fields tools refuse. Every field and value is kept, and switching it on shows them again.

An admin switches Feedback off for a workspace. Off, there is no Feedback in the menu, no way to send feedback or mark up a screen (Ctrl+Shift+M does nothing), and no inbox tool; its addresses say it is switched off. What was sent stays in the builders’ inbox.
An admin switches the Goal map off for a workspace. Off, Goals offers no Map, and a link or saved view that asked for it opens the List and says so.

An admin switches the Wrap-up off for a workspace. Off, nobody is asked how a goal landed (no wrap-up on Home, Goals, a goal or Cycles, no wrap-up page or tool); results are worked out as before and an admin still starts the next year from Cycles. Switching it off first says how many wrap-ups stay. Wrap-ups already written stay in History.

Workspace, Features lists the optional features in groups: Working together (Reviews, Watching, the Wrap-up), Tools (the Metric library, Spreadsheets, the Goal map) and Beyond this workspace (Feedback); a group with nothing installed is not shown. A feature on that holds something says so in a third line (how many reviews are set up, how many people watch goals, when the wrap-up opens). About lists what is on in the same order.

A number is never rounded quietly: one typed with more decimal places than its goal keeps is refused, with what it would show as, in the check-in, New goal, goal edit, the import and the AI tools. Letters in a number get one message everywhere, every number shown has its thousands grouped, and numbers far outside the plan are questioned, never refused.

Two goals may share a title and two people a name (the email is who someone is). Creating one warns; wherever both could be on screen, a goal shows its key and a person their team or job title beside the name, and people with the same initials get different avatar colours.
On the icon rail the Faro mark is the workspace switcher: it opens the same panel as the sidebar's Switch, adds no row (the Demo box keeps its room at 1024 × 768), and Escape returns focus to it.

A module's menu row and a Goals tab wait until they have something in them (a tab also waits while it is the same list as one drawn before it; All is always drawn), in each workspace on its own: a row drawn in one never follows you into another. Hiding is only drawing: every address still opens. Home's sections wait too: “Goals you watch” while nothing is watched, and with one team in the workspace “Your goals” and “Your team” are one section, “The team’s goals · {n}”, the viewer's own first.

No count of nought beside a tab, a menu row or a section's name (a sentence may still say none), and an empty page says what is true, then when you'd want it, with a plain button rather than the page's primary.
